newsitem.title: DENMARK: China postpones Danish minister visits over rights.
newsitem.headline: China postpones Danish minister visits over rights.

text.p: China has postponed scheduled visits by two Danish ministers because of Denmark's support for a U.N. resolution critical of its human rights record, the Danish foreign ministry said on Tuesday.

The ministry said Beijing informed it that planned visits to China by Danish Social Affairs Minister Karen Jespersen in June and Justice Minister Frank Jensen in the autumn had been postponed until further notice.
It said a visit to China by Danish Education Minister Ole Vig Jensen would go ahead as scheduled in May, as would a private visit by Danish Crown Prince Joachim and Princess Alexandra, set for July.

Prince Joachim, younger son of ruling Danish Queen Margrethe, and his Hong Kong-born wife are to attend ceremonies on July 1 formally marking the handing over of the British crown colony to China's control.
The royal couple are to tour China after visiting Hong Kong.
Earlier on Tuesday, the Netherlands Economic Affairs Ministry said China postponed a Dutch trade mission scheduled for June because of its support for the U.N. resolution.

Denmark, with the Netherlands, the United States and 12 other countries, is co-sponsoring a resolution criticising China's human rights record. China has warned that relations with these countries will be affected.
